verdict.rationale: Appwrite documents provisioning managed databases, either on a shared pool or on dedicated compute, including managed PostgreSQL. It also documents TablesDB with typed rows, a CLI that manages rows, generated type-safe SDKs, and many SDKs alongside the REST and GraphQL APIs. However, the evidence never explicitly shows reading and writing database rows from both a client SDK and a server SDK, so coverage of the full story is incomplete. missing for 10: explicit documentation of client-SDK and server-SDK database read/write calls, and independent hands-on corroboration of the provision-then-read/write flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision a managed database and read/write it from client and server SDKs

citations.quote: An Appwrite database runs either on a shared pool that Appwrite manages for you, or on compute provisioned for your project alone.
Choose the database that fits your use case, from managed APIs with permissions and realtime to dedicated native engines you connect to directly.
You can use one of our many SDKs or integrate directly through the REST API or GraphQL API.
It detects your project's language and generates typed helpers based on your database schema.
